title: Analysis of Power Consumption and GPU Power Capping for MILC
problem: Understanding power consumption behavior of MILC lattice quantum chromodynamics application and its performance under GPU power capping constraints on the Perlmutter GPU system.
motivation: Power limitations are becoming critical constraints for supercomputer operations during the exascale era, requiring effective power management methods.
method: The researchers measured power consumption of MILC (a quantum physics simulation program) on a Perlmutter GPU system, testing its Generation and Spectrum components with varying numbers of parallel tasks and different data sizes. They then ran these same tasks with the GPU power limited to different levels and measured the resulting performance changes, characterizing the trade-off between power savings and performance loss.
key_novelty: When MILC's GPU power is reduced to 50% of TDP (maximum design power), performance drops by less than 15%, making it well-suited for power-capping strategies.
contributions: Characterization of MILC power consumption patterns across varying concurrency and input sizes
Analysis of MILC performance degradation under GPU power capping
Demonstration that MILC achieves 50% power reduction with <15% performance loss
Quantification of power-performance trade-off for lattice QCD workloads on GPU systems
limitations: Study focuses specifically on MILC on Perlmutter; generalizability to other applications and systems is not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU power capping for HPC applications
